statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: No, 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show such conduct.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: To satisfy 31 U.S.C. § 5324, there must be evidence that a person structured transactions to evade the reporting requirements of the Bank Secrecy Act (typically by keeping cash deposits under $10,000). In this fact pattern, while there are several cash transactions, there is no evidence of a pattern of splitting larger sums into smaller ones to avoid a Currency Transaction Report (CTR). Specifically, the entity conducted cash transactions of $14,866.01 (2026-02-12) and $16,911.49 (2026-04-30), both of which exceed the $10,000 threshold and would have triggered reporting regardless of other activity. Because the entity is making deposits above the threshold, 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring but the entity is not attempting to evade reporting through structuring.
